articles.title: Overview
articles.description: What StoryWeaver is and how the pieces fit together.

blocks.text: StoryWeaver is a local-first authoring platform and runtime engine for branching visual novels. Stories are built as a directed graph of nodes on a canvas, simulated in-browser via a playtest engine, and compiled out to portable formats — a single-file HTML player or Ren’Py script bundle.

The stack is TypeScript end-to-end: React for the UI, Zustand (+ zundo for undo/redo) for runtime state, Dexie.js over IndexedDB/OPFS for persistence, and Zod for schema validation at every import/export boundary.

items: Story Node Graph — every scene, choice, and rule is a typed node connected by choice edges or direct pointers.
Zustand Runtime Store — the single source of truth for the currently loaded project, both while editing and while playtesting.
Dexie Persistence Layer — projects, nodes, variables, characters, items, and binary assets all live in IndexedDB tables.
Playtest Simulator — runs the graph exactly as a player would experience it, without leaving the editor.
Exporters — deterministic compilers from the node graph to a standalone HTML player or a Ren’Py script bundle.

blocks.title: Academic context
blocks.text: This engine doubles as a Computer Science senior project — every non-trivial implementation session is logged under AI_Prompt_Logs/ for thesis evaluation, cross-linked to the underlying CS theory in the project wiki.

articles.title: Quickstart Guide
articles.description: From a blank workspace to a playable branching scene in five steps.

sections.heading: Five Steps to a Playable Scene

items: Open /dashboard and click New Project — or clone a starter template to skip straight to a working example.
Drag a node from the Nodes Catalog onto the canvas, or click a catalog entry to spawn it at a default position.
Wire the story together: drag from a node’s choice handle to the node you want it to lead to.
Open Playtest to simulate the graph exactly as a player would see it — dialogue, gated choices, inventory, all live.
Export when ready — either a single-file HTML player or a Ren’Py script bundle.

blocks.title: Fastest path
blocks.text: Cloning a starter template from the Dashboard’s template panel gives you a fully-wired, playable graph in one click — useful for learning node wiring by example.

articles.title: Local-First Philosophy
articles.description: Why every project lives entirely in your browser, and what that means for backups.

blocks.text: StoryWeaver has no application server. Every project — nodes, variables, characters, items, and binary assets like cover art or audio — is persisted client-side via Dexie.js on top of IndexedDB. Larger binary payloads are promoted to the Origin Private File System (OPFS) to avoid the ~5MB ceiling that plain localStorage imposes.

rows: nodes, variables, characters, items, project metadata

blocks.title: Nothing is uploaded
blocks.text: Because there is no backend, clearing your browser’s site data for this origin permanently deletes every local project. Export a JSON backup regularly from the Dashboard if a story matters to you.

articles.title: Start Node
articles.description: The single entrypoint of a story graph.

blocks.text: Every story graph has exactly one Start node — the entrypoint the playtest engine and every exporter begin traversal from. It behaves like any linear node: its text renders, then flow continues to whatever its first choice (or nextNodeId) points at.

rows: Discriminates this node in the shared StoryNode union.
Opening narration shown before the first choice.
The node that follows the opening beat.

articles.title: Dialogue & Narration Nodes
articles.description: The two text-presentation node types — spoken lines and scene description.

blocks.text: Dialogue nodes present a character-spoken line, typically alongside a portrait asset. Narration nodes present unattributed descriptive text — scene-setting, internal monologue, prose between beats. Both share the same underlying shape: a text body and a choices[] array of outgoing branches.

rows: Selects presentation style in the player.
Reference to a StoryAsset for the scene background.
Outgoing branches; a single unconditioned choice acts as a "Continue" beat.

articles.title: Choice & Branching
articles.description: How outgoing edges are modeled, and how they can be gated.

blocks.text: A "Choice" is not a separate node type — it’s an entry in a node’s choices[] array. Each choice points at a target node and can optionally carry a ChoiceCondition that gates its visibility at runtime via the engine’s evaluateCondition() helper.

blocks.title: Gated choices in the simulator
blocks.text: During playtest, a choice whose condition evaluates to false is rendered locked rather than hidden — the player sees the branch exists but can’t select it yet.

articles.title: Action Node
articles.description: Mutates global variables or inventory without pausing for player input.

blocks.text: Action nodes run automatically as the engine passes through them. data.actionType selects the operation, and data.payload carries its arguments. set_variable actions additionally read an operator (=, +=, -=) so the same node type covers assignment and arithmetic.

rows: Assigns, increments, or decrements a global variable.
Adds an item; stackable items increment quantity instead of duplicating.
Removes a matching item entry from inventory.

blocks.text: minConstraint and failureNodeId turn a plain decrement into a guarded transaction: if subtracting would cross the floor, the engine reroutes to the failure branch instead of committing a negative balance.

articles.title: Condition Node
articles.description: Two-way branching based on a variable comparison.

blocks.text: Condition nodes carry a single ChoiceCondition at data.condition and two outgoing pointers, trueTargetNodeId and falseTargetNodeId. The engine evaluates the condition once and routes deterministically — no player-facing choice is rendered.

rows: Substring match (strings) or membership match (inventory arrays)

articles.title: Subgraphs
articles.description: Grouping related nodes into a nested canvas scope.

blocks.text: A Sub-Graph Folder node groups a set of child nodes under a shared parentGroupId, giving them a nested canvas scope. Double-clicking the folder opens its contents; this keeps large branching stories organized instead of flattening every node onto one unbounded canvas.

blocks.title: Organizing large stories
blocks.text: Use subgraphs to isolate self-contained arcs — a side quest, a chapter, a minigame — so the top-level canvas stays readable as the story grows.

articles.title: Input Node
articles.description: Pauses the story for a player-typed value — the basis of a character creation form.

blocks.text: Input nodes pause traversal for a text or numeric prompt and write the player’s response into a variable — the pattern used to build a character-naming or trait-selection form at story start. data.targetVariable names the variable to write, data.placeholder sets the prompt hint, and data.characterName optionally labels who is asking.

rows: Variable key the typed value is written into.
Hint text shown in the empty input field.
Optional speaker label for the prompt.

articles.title: Variable Registry
articles.description: The typed schema behind a project’s global variable bag.

blocks.text: StoryVariable rows declare a project’s typed variable schema — key, type, and defaultValue. At runtime, the Zustand store’s variables record is seeded from these defaults on project load (and on a reset), then mutated live by Action and Condition nodes as the player progresses.

rows: Identifier; must match a valid variable-name pattern.
Declared type, enforced at authoring time.
Seed value used when a new game state is created.

articles.title: JIT Math Evaluator
articles.description: How Action nodes resolve arithmetic at traversal time, not authoring time.

blocks.text: Variable arithmetic is resolved just-in-time as the engine steps through an Action node, not baked in when the story is authored. The += and -= operators coerce both the currently stored value and the incoming payload to numbers on the fly, then apply an optional minConstraint floor — with a += or -= that would cross the floor rerouting to failureNodeId instead of committing.

blocks.title: Type coercion
blocks.text: Because operands are coerced with Number(...), a non-numeric stored value is treated as 0 before the operator applies — arithmetic never throws mid-traversal.

articles.title: Stackable Inventory Pouch
articles.description: How add/remove inventory actions handle stackable vs. unique items.

blocks.text: Inventory is a flat array of item entries on the game state. add_inventory actions check the stackable flag: stackable items increment a shared quantity field on an existing matching entry instead of pushing a duplicate; non-stackable items always push a new entry. Display metadata (name, image) is cached separately in runtimeItemCatalog so the HUD can render without re-joining against the item table on every frame.

rows: Runtime array of held items, keyed by item id.
Cached display metadata for the inventory HUD.

articles.title: Simulator Viewport
articles.description: Running the story graph exactly as a player would experience it.

blocks.text: PlaytestOverlayStage renders GamePlayerPortal full-bleed over the editor canvas, simulating the graph with the same traversal engine used at runtime — dialogue advancement, choice gating via evaluateCondition(), and the live inventory HUD — all without leaving the current editing session.

articles.title: Real-time Debug Panel
articles.description: Inspecting live variable and inventory state mid-playtest.

blocks.text: DebugToolbar exposes the current variables record and inventory contents while a playtest session is running, toggled with a keybind so it stays out of the way until you need it. It’s read-only telemetry — a window into engine state, not a state editor.

blocks.title: Diagnosing a stuck branch
blocks.text: If a choice looks permanently locked, open the debug panel first — it usually means the guarding variable never got set by the Action node upstream.

articles.title: Time-Travel Undo/Redo
articles.description: How editor history is kept separate from playtest runtime state.

blocks.text: The canvas editor’s Zustand store is wrapped in zundo’s temporal() middleware, giving every node and edge mutation an undo/redo stack for free. That history is explicitly cleared via temporal.getState().clear() around non-undoable transitions — like starting a fresh playtest session — so gameplay state changes never leak into the editor’s undo timeline.

articles.title: Single-file HTML Web Exporter
articles.description: A self-contained, offline-playable build of a story.

blocks.text: The web exporter bundles a story’s nodes, embedded assets, and a standalone traversal engine into a single .html file — a self-contained visual-novel player that runs offline in any browser with no server, install step, or external dependency.

articles.title: Ren’Py Script Middleware
articles.description: Compiling the node graph down to Ren’Py’s own scripting language.

blocks.text: renpyExporter.ts walks the node graph via an adjacency map and re-emits it as .rpy script files — labels, jump targets, menu blocks for choices, and $ statements for variable assignment — letting a story authored visually in StoryWeaver compile down to a project the Ren’Py engine can run directly.

blocks.code:
label node_start:
    "The story opens here."
    jump node_2

label node_2:
    menu:
        "Continue":
            jump node_3

articles.title: Zod JSON Contract Specs
articles.description: The runtime-validated schema every export/import round-trip must satisfy.

blocks.text: Every export and import path is validated against Zod schemas — storyNodeSchema, storyVariableSchema, and the top-level storyWeaverExportSchema envelope — before it touches disk or the local Dexie database. A malformed backup fails fast with a readable Zod error instead of silently corrupting local project data.
